overview: This file documents a May–July 1937 complaint by the Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America that Japanese postal authorities had delayed, opened, and read mail sent from the United States to the Tokyo manager of United Artists Corporation. The State Department referred the allegation to the American Consul General in Tokyo, whose investigation found the suspicion plausible but learned that the manager, A. A. Lowe, had intended only to inform his home office and did not want official action. Consular officials noted similar complaints from other Americans, including suspicions about consular mail, but believed that representations to Japanese authorities would be futile without definite proof; they also suggested that unusually large consolidated envelopes might be examined because they could be suspected of containing motion-picture films imported without censorship. The correspondence concludes with the Department reporting these findings to Frederick L. Herron and Herron apologizing for the failure of the United Artists representative to clarify or pursue his complaint.

subfiles.title: Herron complaint concerning United Artists mail in Tokyo
subfiles.from: Frederick L. Herron, Motion Picture Producers and Distributors of America, Inc.
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Department of State
subfiles.about: Herron reports that Japanese authorities have allegedly delayed, opened, and read mail addressed to the United Artists manager in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Herron asks Hornbeck to investigate reports that a United Artists manager's mail was opened and read in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck reply promising a consular investigation
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges Herron's complaint and states that the American Consul General in Tokyo will investigate it.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck tells Herron the consul in Tokyo will investigate the alleged mail tampering.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Consul General Garrels to investigate
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Arthur Garrels, American Consul General in Tokyo
subfiles.about: The State Department directs Garrels to investigate the United Artists complaint and, if warranted, approach the local postal authorities.
subfiles.summary: State instructs Consul Garrels to investigate the United Artists mail-tampering allegation in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Herron clarification concerning the Tokyo complaint
subfiles.about: Herron clarifies that the United Artists representative complained to the Tokyo post office but apparently did not approach the American Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Herron clarifies the complaint went to Tokyo's post office, not the American Embassy.

subfiles.title: Consul General Garrels's report on alleged mail tampering
subfiles.about: Garrels reports the results of his interview with A. A. Lowe and explains why the Consulate General will take no further action.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports the United Artists manager regrets raising the complaint and wants no action, though mail scrutiny was likely, possibly over suspected smuggled film.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck reports the consular findings to Herron
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hornbeck informs Herron that the Consulate General found insufficient evidence for official representations and that Lowe had requested no action.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck relays Garrels's findings to Herron: mail tampering was likely but unprovable, and the complainant asked that no action be taken.

subfiles.title: Herron's acknowledgment and apology
subfiles.about: Herron thanks Hornbeck for obtaining the report and apologizes for the United Artists representative's failure to follow up his complaint.
subfiles.summary: Herron thanks Hornbeck and apologizes that the complainant never properly pursued the matter.

interest: Shows a 1930s US firm's mail-tampering complaint in Japan, dropped for lack of proof despite official suspicion.
